text:
Liam O'Brien is a fourth-line enforcer in the old sense, an undrafted 32-year-old who has made 265 NHL games out of hits and hard minutes. He's played eight games for Utah this season, under eight minutes a night, and thrown 34 hits in that time, more than four a game.

He hasn't scored, but he's had a couple of looks: 1.06 expected goals (the quality of chances) on his own shots, which is a lot for his ice time. Utah takes 58% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, about the team rate, so his shifts aren't costing the Mammoth anything. With the injuries up front, he's been dressing more regularly.

Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, in a small sample, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a player who dumps the puck in and goes to work (27% carry-ins). Our model's closest comparisons are Jacob Melanson and Curtis Douglas, big depth forwards who block and hit. Our talent range has him around 6 goals if he plays the rest of the way, which he probably won't. His value is in the corners, and on a team winless in five, that counts for something.
